persona.goal: quality filter on mixed stereo/mono input
persona.opening_prompt: I've got a mix of stereo and mono clips and I just want to keep the clean, good-sounding ones.
persona.persona_facts: Some files are stereo, some mono; English.
persona.preferences: When asked the quality level, say general.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I've got a mix of stereo and mono clips and I just want to keep the clean, good-sounding ones.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
I've mapped the request to a **quality-filter** task and inspected the catalog. A few grounded findings:

- Your stereo/mono mix needs normalizing first — `MonoConversionStage` is the standard front of a quality chain (the MOS models are speech, mono, 16 kHz).
- For "clean **and** good-sounding", `SIGMOSFilterStage` is the best fit: unlike `UTMOSFilterStage` (a single overall MOS), SIGMOS scores both a **noise** dimension ("clean") and an **overall** dimension ("good-sounding") in one stage. I'd recommend it.

The one thing I can't infer is **how strict** "good-sounding" should be — this sets the keep/reject bar and how much of your data survives, and it's a preference call, so I don't want to pick a threshold for you.

**How clean/good do the kept clips need to be?**
- **Studio** — only pristine, near-flawless clips (keeps the least)
- **General** — solid, clearly usable clips (a sensible middle ground)
- **Lenient** — just drop the obviously bad ones (keeps the most)

Once you pick a level, I'll `resolve` it to the exact SIGMOS thresholds, `validate`, and hand you the runnable recipe.

card.summary: Predict UTMOS mean-opinion-score (MOS) and filter/annotate audio by quality.

resource.throughput_hint: fast on GPU; CPU fallback is slower

good_for: gate speech clips by overall perceptual quality
TTS/ASR data curation
avoid_for: music or non-speech
very short (<1s) clips

params_of_note.mos_threshold: minimum MOS to keep (0-5). TTS: >=4.0; ASR/general: >=3.4; max retention: >=2.5
params_of_note.action: 'filter' drops below threshold; 'annotate' keeps all and only writes the score

comparison.accuracy_hint: single overall MOS predictor; coarser than SIGMOS's 7 dimensions
comparison.known_limitations: predictor of human MOS, not a ground-truth measurement; speech-only

caveats: Downloads the model from torch.hub on first run (needs network once).
Score is a predictor of human MOS, not a ground-truth measurement.

card.summary: SIGMOS (ITU-T P.804) neural MOS across 7 quality dimensions; filter/annotate.

resource.throughput_hint: ONNX; uses GPU if available, CPU fallback

good_for: fine-grained quality gating (noise, reverb, discontinuity, loudness, coloration)
TTS data curation
avoid_for: non-speech audio

params_of_note.noise_threshold: min NOISE score to keep (0-5); 4.0 keeps only very-low-noise clips
params_of_note.ovrl_threshold: min OVRL (overall) score to keep (0-5); single best general-purpose gate
params_of_note.sig_threshold: optional min SIG (signal) score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.col_threshold: optional min COL (coloration) score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.disc_threshold: optional min DISC (discontinuity) score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.loud_threshold: optional min LOUD (loudness) score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.reverb_threshold: optional min REVERB score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.action: 'filter' drops below threshold(s); 'annotate' keeps all and writes scores

comparison.accuracy_hint: 7-dimension P.804 MOS; finer-grained than UTMOS's single score
comparison.known_limitations: speech-only; empirically the most aggressive filter (drops the most rows)

notes: Writes all 7 scores (sigmos_noise, sigmos_ovrl, sigmos_sig, sigmos_col, sigmos_disc, sigmos_loud, sigmos_reverb) regardless of active thresholds, so you can post-filter.
Empirically the most aggressive quality filter -- place last in a cheap->expensive filter chain, or first for maximum early cull.
caveats: Downloads the ONNX model on first run (needs network once).

card.summary: Predict UTMOS mean-opinion-score (MOS) and filter/annotate audio by quality.

resource.throughput_hint: fast on GPU; CPU fallback is slower

good_for: gate speech clips by overall perceptual quality
TTS/ASR data curation
avoid_for: music or non-speech
very short (<1s) clips

params_of_note.mos_threshold: minimum MOS to keep (0-5). TTS: >=4.0; ASR/general: >=3.4; max retention: >=2.5
params_of_note.action: 'filter' drops below threshold; 'annotate' keeps all and only writes the score

comparison.accuracy_hint: single overall MOS predictor; coarser than SIGMOS's 7 dimensions
comparison.known_limitations: predictor of human MOS, not a ground-truth measurement; speech-only

caveats: Downloads the model from torch.hub on first run (needs network once).
Score is a predictor of human MOS, not a ground-truth measurement.

card.summary: SIGMOS (ITU-T P.804) neural MOS across 7 quality dimensions; filter/annotate.

resource.throughput_hint: ONNX; uses GPU if available, CPU fallback

good_for: fine-grained quality gating (noise, reverb, discontinuity, loudness, coloration)
TTS data curation
avoid_for: non-speech audio

params_of_note.noise_threshold: min NOISE score to keep (0-5); 4.0 keeps only very-low-noise clips
params_of_note.ovrl_threshold: min OVRL (overall) score to keep (0-5); single best general-purpose gate
params_of_note.sig_threshold: optional min SIG (signal) score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.col_threshold: optional min COL (coloration) score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.disc_threshold: optional min DISC (discontinuity) score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.loud_threshold: optional min LOUD (loudness) score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.reverb_threshold: optional min REVERB score to keep (0-5)
params_of_note.action: 'filter' drops below threshold(s); 'annotate' keeps all and writes scores

comparison.accuracy_hint: 7-dimension P.804 MOS; finer-grained than UTMOS's single score
comparison.known_limitations: speech-only; empirically the most aggressive filter (drops the most rows)

notes: Writes all 7 scores (sigmos_noise, sigmos_ovrl, sigmos_sig, sigmos_col, sigmos_disc, sigmos_loud, sigmos_reverb) regardless of active thresholds, so you can post-filter.
Empirically the most aggressive quality filter -- place last in a cheap->expensive filter chain, or first for maximum early cull.
caveats: Downloads the ONNX model on first run (needs network once).
